config.title: Colors: hex, rgb, hsl

intro.title: Colors: hex, rgb, hsl
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage that displays a set of colored boxes, each labeled with a different color format. You will learn the core concepts of specifying colors in CSS using three common methods: hexadecimal (hex), RGB (Red, Green, Blue), and HSL (Hue, Saturation, Lightness). The main technologies involved are CSS properties like `color` and `background-color`, along with their respective value formats. By the end, you'll be able to apply and compare these color formats to style text and backgrounds effectively.
intro.usecase: Color systems are foundational to every visual interface developers build. When creating design systems for products like dashboards or e-commerce platforms, you'll use hex codes for precise brand colors, RGB for dynamic theming (like dark/light mode), and HSL for intuitive color adjustments in UI components. For example, a weather app might use HSL to smoothly transition sky colors throughout the day, while an admin panel uses hex values to maintain consistent button and text colors across all modules. Mastering these color formats lets you implement professional designs exactly as specified by designers and create visually cohesive user experiences.

objectives: Apply hexadecimal color values to style text and background properties
Configure RGB color values with varying opacity levels using rgba()
Construct HSL color values to adjust hue, saturation, and lightness independently
Manipulate color properties across multiple HTML elements using different color formats
Implement color transitions by updating CSS custom properties with hex, rgb, and hsl values
Integrate multiple color formats within a single stylesheet to maintain consistency
Control color inheritance by applying specific color formats to parent and child elements

steps.title: Create a CSS file and add a basic HTML structure
steps.instruction: Create a new CSS file and add a basic HTML structure with a container and three color boxes. Start by writing the HTML structure in your CSS file using comments to outline the elements.
steps.hint: You can use CSS comments (/* */) to describe the HTML elements you'll be styling. This helps organize your CSS by mapping it to your HTML structure.
steps.seedCode: /* Create your HTML structure in comments here */
steps.expectedOutcome: Your CSS file will have a commented outline of the HTML structure with a container and three color boxes, ready for styling.
successCriteria: The CSS file contains comments describing a container div with three box divs inside it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your comments include a container div with three box divs inside. Check the example for reference.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's start from the beginning. Create a CSS file and add comments that describe an HTML structure with a container and three color boxes.

steps.title: Add basic styling to the container and boxes
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for the container class to use flexbox for layout, and add rules for the box class to give them dimensions and borders.
steps.hint: Use display: flex for the container, and set width, height, and border properties for the boxes.
steps.seedCode:
/* Create your HTML structure in comments here */

/* Add your CSS rules below */
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will use flexbox layout, and the boxes will have visible dimensions and borders.
successCriteria: CSS rules for .container and .box are added with flexbox, dimensions, and borders.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both .container and .box rules are present with the required properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The styling is missing or incomplete. Check that you've added CSS rules for both the container and boxes.

steps.title: Apply HEX color to the first box
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule to set the background-color of the first box using the HEX color code #FF5733.
steps.hint: Target the first box using its class selector and set the background-color property to #FF5733.
steps.expectedOutcome: The first box should have a vibrant orange background color (#FF5733).
successCriteria: The first box has a background-color property set to #FF5733.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the HEX code is exactly #FF5733.
steps.feedbackWrong: The first box doesn't have the correct HEX color. Check that you're targeting the first box and using #FF5733.

steps.title: Add color labels with text styling
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS rule for a class named 'label' that sets font properties and text alignment.
steps.hint: Create a new CSS selector for .label and add properties like font-family, font-size, font-weight, and text-align.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule for .label is created with at least three font/text styling properties.
successCriteria: The CSS contains a .label selector with properties for font-family, font-size, and text-align (or similar text styling properties).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a .label rule, but it needs more text styling properties. Try adding at least three properties like font-family, font-size, and text-align.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS doesn't contain a .label rule with text styling properties. Create a new CSS rule for .label with font and text alignment properties.

steps.title: Create hover effects with different color formats
steps.instruction: Add a hover effect to the first box that changes its background color to a different HEX value when hovered.
steps.hint: Use the :hover pseudo-class on the .box selector to change the background-color property to a new HEX color like #ff6347.
steps.expectedOutcome: The first box will change to a different HEX color when you hover over it.
successCriteria: A :hover rule for .box is added with a background-color set to a different HEX value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a hover effect, but make sure to use a HEX color value for the background-color.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hover effect is missing or incorrect. Try adding .box:hover { background-color: #ff6347; }

steps.title: Add transparency with RGBA and HSLA
steps.instruction: Create a fourth box with the class 'box-transparent' and apply a background color with transparency using RGBA.
steps.hint: Add a new CSS rule for .box-transparent with width, height, border, and background-color using rgba(red, green, blue, alpha) where alpha is between 0 and 1.
steps.expectedOutcome: A fourth box appears with a semi-transparent background color using RGBA.
successCriteria: A .box-transparent rule is created with width, height, border, and background-color using rgba() with an alpha value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the .box-transparent rule, but make sure to include background-color with rgba() and an alpha value between 0 and 1.
steps.feedbackWrong: The transparent box rule is missing or incorrect. Create a .box-transparent class with width, height, border, and background-color using rgba().

steps.title: Style text with different color formats
steps.instruction: Add a heading and paragraph to your HTML structure (in comments) and style them using HEX, RGB, and HSL color formats respectively.
steps.hint: Create a heading element with HEX color, a paragraph with RGB color, and another paragraph with HSL color. Add these styles to your CSS.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have added CSS rules to style text elements with HEX, RGB, and HSL color formats.
successCriteria: CSS includes rules for a heading with HEX color, a paragraph with RGB color, and another paragraph with HSL color.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some text styling, but make sure to include all three color formats: HEX, RGB, and HSL.
steps.feedbackWrong: The text styling is missing or doesn't use the required color formats. Try adding rules for heading and paragraphs with HEX, RGB, and HSL colors.

steps.title: Add borders with different color formats
steps.instruction: Add a border to each box using a different color format: use HEX for the first box, RGB for the second, and HSL for the third.
steps.hint: Use the border property with different color values. For example: border: 4px solid #ff5733;
steps.expectedOutcome: Each box will have a distinct border color using HEX, RGB, and HSL formats.
successCriteria: All three boxes have borders with different color formats: HEX, RGB, and HSL.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added borders, but make sure each box uses a different color format: HEX, RGB, and HSL.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you added borders to all three boxes with the correct color formats.
